nodes.label: Skill Authoring Workspace
nodes.rationale: Central workspace for building, editing, evaluating, and demoing Claude AI Skills. Skills are small, triggered playbooks that get loaded into Claude's context when a relevant task comes up.

nodes.label: Skill Install Flow
nodes.rationale: Each .skill file is a zip of its source folder. Install by dropping the folder into a local skills directory, importing through Cowork plugin UI, or syncing into a plugin source repo.

nodes.label: Progressive Disclosure Pattern
nodes.rationale: Frontmatter pre-loaded every session; SKILL.md body loaded on trigger; references loaded on demand. This is the entire reason the system scales to dozens of skills without flooding context.

nodes.label: Eval-First Authoring Principle
nodes.rationale: Three evals before SKILL.md body is written. Anticipatory documentation is the failure mode this prevents. Skills written in a vacuum drift.

nodes.label: Trigger Eval Format
nodes.rationale: Flat top-level JSON array with query, should_trigger, optional category. No wrapper object. 10 should-fire and 10 should-not-fire. Negatives are near-misses, not obvious noise.

nodes.label: Loop Results Persistence Pattern
nodes.rationale: Run-loop summary saved to <skill>/evals/loop-results.md. Raw output gitignored. Summary captures date, model, scores, best description, decision, patterns.

nodes.label: HTML Demo Public GitHub Safety Contract
nodes.rationale: No API keys, no process.env, no provider endpoints, no PII. Single-file HTML, runs from file://, pure client-side compute by default. If LLM calls needed, use user-pasted key stored in localStorage only.
nodes.norm_label: html demo public github safety contract

nodes.label: Gerund Naming Convention
nodes.rationale: Folder name = frontmatter name field = slash-command trigger = gerund. One canonical string per skill. Short-trigger/long-name split was abandoned because it created two strings for one identity.

nodes.label: SKILL.md 500-Line Cap
nodes.rationale: Body cap of 500 lines. Past that, split into references/<topic>.md one level deep. Never nest references.

nodes.label: Complexity Ladder Test
nodes.rationale: Walk the architecture up the ladder; stop at the lowest rung that meets requirements. Principal-grade advice often reduces complexity. Referenced in architectural-tradeoffs.md.

nodes.label: Post-Creation Handoff Magic Line
nodes.rationale: Exact handoff message after skill completion. Magic line doubles as a discovery test: if Claude doesn't recognize the skill name after installation, the description is broken.

nodes.label: Pattern-Recognition Cue
nodes.rationale: Closes every explanation with one line: 'Next time you see a problem like this, the signal to look for is: [X].' Makes each explanation transferable to a class of problems, not just one-off.

nodes.label: explaining vs working-through Conflict
nodes.rationale: The two skills are mutually exclusive. If both are available, ask user to pick. If /working-through is not in available skills list, treat request as /explaining directly without asking.

nodes.label: Mode Routing Table
nodes.rationale: 5 modes: Solution-Design, Architecture, Engineering Deep-Dive, Evaluation/Ops, Governance. Same domain can be discussed at any level. Adapt depth accordingly.

nodes.label: 6-Step Core Response Framework
nodes.rationale: Frame → Pattern → Stack → Failure Modes → Eval & Ops → Path to Production. Never skip framing. Can compress when question is narrow.

nodes.label: Knowledge Currency Mechanism
nodes.rationale: Check references/knowledge-version.md at start. If >14 days stale, mention to user. Patterns endure, tools change. When in doubt about tool/vendor, search the web.

nodes.label: Refresh Cadence Design
nodes.rationale: Twice-weekly recommended. Tool/vendor specifics change in 4-8 weeks. Patterns endure. Don't replace durable decision trees just because vendor news appears.

nodes.label: POC-to-Production Path
nodes.rationale: Phase 0 (pre-POC, validated use case + baseline) → Phase 1 (functional POC) → Phase 2 (production-quality + shadow mode) → Phase 3 (rollout) → Phase 4 (continuous improvement). Common failure mode: skipping Phase 0.

nodes.label: Build vs Buy Decision Tree
nodes.rationale: Buy if vertical SaaS solves exact use case without unique data advantage. Build if it's a competitive differentiator or the team has depth. Multi-model strategy (81% of enterprises run 3+ families) for cost optimization and risk diversification.

nodes.label: Use Case Validation Framework
nodes.rationale: 4-question framework: Is it a real problem? Is AI the right lever? What's the value at stake? What could go wrong? LLMs are right for ambiguous language, judgment under partial info, generation, multi-step reasoning.

nodes.label: Complexity Ladder (10 Rungs)
nodes.rationale: Rung 1: one LLM call → Rung 10: Temporal + agent. Most production systems live at rung 4-6. Conference talks describe 7-9. Principal asks: what specific failure of rung N-1 forced you to rung N?

nodes.label: RAG Honest Hierarchy
nodes.rationale: Naive RAG fails ~40% in real corpora. Hybrid+rerank+contextual retrieval is new production baseline. Agentic RAG mostly overkill. The 73% rule: when RAG fails it's retrieval 73% of the time.

nodes.label: Don't Add That List
nodes.rationale: Principal-grade advisor stops things from being built. Key entries: multi-agent before single-agent ceiling, vector DB before BM25 test, GraphRAG before measuring multi-hop share, reflection loops before measuring quality ceiling, fine-tuning before exhausting prompt+RAG.

nodes.label: Five Architecture Review Questions
nodes.rationale: 1. Simplest design that could plausibly work? 2. Eval set + baseline? 3. What specific failure mode does this layer prevent? 4. What fails first at 10x? 5. What's the rollback?

nodes.label: Overhyped vs Underhyped 2026
nodes.rationale: Overhyped: agentic framing on workflows, GraphRAG as universal upgrade, multi-agent as default, fine-tuning for quality issues, self-hosting as cost optimization. Underhyped: contextual retrieval (35-50% lift), routing patterns (60-80% cost savings), eval discipline, prompt caching, boring workflows.

nodes.label: Evaluation Discipline
nodes.rationale: Component-level → End-to-end → Production/online evals. 50-100 examples to start, representative not exhaustive. LLM-as-judge: pairwise over absolute scoring, stronger model as judge, rubric in prompt, spot-check against humans.

nodes.label: Data Flywheel Pattern
nodes.rationale: Dev eval datasets + production traces → feedback → annotated failures → new test cases → improved prompts/retrieval/models. This distinguishes shipping projects from production-grade systems.

nodes.label: Cost Optimization Order of Operations
nodes.rationale: 1. Prompt caching (50-90% win) → 2. Right-size models → 3. Reduce context → 4. Limit max_tokens → 5. Cache responses → 6. Batch async work → 7. Self-host. Don't skip steps.

nodes.label: RAG Pattern Spectrum
nodes.rationale: Naive → Advanced (production baseline) → GraphRAG → Agentic RAG → Adaptive RAG. Match query complexity to pipeline complexity. Naive RAG fails retrieval ~40% in real corpora.

nodes.label: Advanced RAG Pattern
nodes.rationale: Hybrid (BM25 + dense vector + RRF) + cross-encoder reranker + query transformation + source metadata. New production baseline. Typical lift over naive: 15-30% on RAGAS metrics.

nodes.label: Adaptive RAG Pattern
nodes.rationale: Query classifier routes to appropriate pipeline (simple_factual → naive, single_doc → advanced, relationship → graph, multi_step → agentic). Emerging best practice for 2026 mixed workloads.

nodes.label: Chunking Strategy Table
nodes.rationale: Fixed-size, sentence-based, paragraph-based, semantic, parent-child, recursive character. Parent-child gives best precision-context trade-off for long documents. Chunking matters more than embedding model in most cases.

nodes.label: Cascading vs Speech-to-Speech Architecture
nodes.rationale: Cascading (STT→LLM→TTS): best-of-breed per stage, vendor flexibility, lower cost. Speech-to-speech: lower latency, preserves prosody. 2026 reality: cascading still default. Use S2S when latency <500ms or emotional nuance is differentiator.

nodes.label: Voice Agent Latency Budget
nodes.rationale: ~800ms voice-to-voice for natural feel. Audio capture: ~50ms, VAD: ~50ms, STT: ~150ms, LLM TTFT: ~300ms, TTS first audio: ~75-200ms, transport out: ~50ms.

nodes.label: Financial Services AI Playbook
nodes.rationale: Key patterns: fraud detection (rules+classifier+LLM+HITL), KYC/AML (OCR+extraction+classifier+reviewer), regulatory compliance Q&A (GraphRAG), risk decisioning (high-risk EU AI Act, full governance). Sovereign/regional deployment often required.

nodes.label: Healthcare AI Playbook
nodes.rationale: HITL mandatory for any clinical decision. Medical hallucinations cause patient harm. HIPAA, FDA, EU AI Act high-risk. Self-hosted or BAA-protected APIs only for patient data. Medical scribe via real-time transcription+structured extraction is leading pattern.

nodes.label: Customer Support Standard Pattern
nodes.rationale: Pre-LLM guardrails → intent classifier → adaptive RAG router (FAQ/complex/out-of-scope) → LLM generation → post-LLM guardrails → HITL triggers. MCP-exposed CRM/ticketing/KB tools.

nodes.label: 2026 Coding Agent Landscape
nodes.rationale: Categories: terminal-native (Claude Code), IDE-native (Cursor), CLI (Codex CLI), VS Code extension (Cline), terminal minimalist (Aider), cloud agent platform (Devin), enterprise on-prem (Tabnine/Augment). Typical pro setup: Cursor for daily flow + Claude Code for hard problems.

nodes.label: SWE-bench Benchmark Reality
nodes.rationale: SWE-bench Verified is contaminated; SWE-bench Pro is trustworthy. Harness quality matters as much as model (17-point spread on same model across harnesses). Always specify which version when discussing benchmarks.

nodes.label: MCP Tool-Agent Decoupling
nodes.rationale: Every major coding agent except Aider speaks MCP. Agent layer and tool layer are now decoupled — can switch from Cursor to Claude Code without losing tool integrations.

nodes.label: Pre/Post LLM Guardrail Architecture
nodes.rationale: Pre-LLM: prompt injection, PII redaction, topic drift, toxic content, token/cost bombs. Post-LLM: schema compliance, hallucination signals, PII in output, toxic content, refusal detection, length/format compliance, instruction leakage. Never return raw LLM output in production.

nodes.label: Layered Hallucination Defenses
nodes.rationale: Layer 1: prompting (cite context, express confidence). Layer 2: retrieval grounding (refuse when retrieval scores low). Layer 3: output validation (schema, citation verification, NLI entailment). Layer 4: architectural (CoVe, self-consistency, constrained output).

nodes.label: Structured Output Methods
nodes.rationale: 100% guaranteed compliance: constrained decoding (local) or Instructor+Pydantic with retry (closed API). 'Usually correct': native JSON mode + Pydantic validation. Instructor is recommended default for frontier APIs.

nodes.label: Reasoning Model Usage Decision Tree
nodes.rationale: Strong fits: math, code with verifiable tests, scientific Q&A, strategic planning, high-stakes verification. Poor fits: high-volume customer chat, simple extraction, real-time decisioning, conversational interfaces.

nodes.label: Reasoning Router Pattern
nodes.rationale: Dominant 2026 production pattern: classifier routes simple queries to standard model, complex to reasoning model. Cuts cost 60-80% while maintaining 95%+ quality. Router can be few-shot prompt.

nodes.label: Reasoning Distillation Pattern
nodes.rationale: Capture reasoning traces from large reasoning model, SFT smaller base model on those traces. DeepSeek-R1-Distill-Qwen3-8B is canonical: 8B outperforms much larger general models on reasoning benchmarks. Path to reasoning-quality at small-model cost.

nodes.label: Model Tiers Q2 2026
nodes.rationale: Frontier reasoning (Claude Opus 4.x, GPT-5/o-series, Gemini 2.5 Pro), Frontier general (Claude Sonnet 4.x, GPT-4o), Fast/Small (Haiku 4.x, GPT-4o-mini, Gemini Flash), Open-weight large (Llama 3.x/4, DeepSeek-V3, Qwen 3.x), SLMs (Phi-3/4, Llama-3-8B). Always search before quoting.

nodes.label: Prompting Strategy Hierarchy
nodes.rationale: Try in order: zero-shot → few-shot → chain-of-thought → structured decomposition → tool use → agentic loop → fine-tuning. Stop at the level that meets accuracy target. Fine-tuning only after prompt/RAG has plateaued with ≥500 quality examples.

nodes.label: Context Window Management
nodes.rationale: Budget: system prompt <2K, retrieved context 60-80%, conversation history 10-20%, query+output buffer rest. Strategies when full: sliding window, conversation summarization, episodic memory retrieval, contextual compression, map-reduce, tool-based access.

nodes.label: AI vs Traditional Software Production Differences
nodes.rationale: 4 real differences: quality failures are silent (no 5xx), non-deterministic execution (full trace needed), cost is first-class metric, model/provider risk (provider can change behavior under you).
nodes.norm_label: ai vs traditional software production differences

nodes.label: AI SLI/SLO Design
nodes.rationale: 4 SLI categories: Availability, Quality (faithfulness, relevance, citation accuracy), Cost (cost per task, cache hit rate), Decision Quality (task success rate, steps, escalation accuracy). Set SLO at p10 of 30-day observation baseline.

nodes.label: Agent Sprawl Prevention
nodes.rationale: 70%+ of orgs run 3+ models, model debt accumulates. Controls: model registry with named owner + SLO + 30-day baseline, deprecation monitoring like CVEs (60/30/7 day alerts), periodic retirement reviews, standard observability across all models.
